points.description: Defines frame bursting as concatenating/sending a sequence of multiple frames in one single transmission (burst), WITHOUT releasing control of the channel in between.
points.partial_credit: Half (0.2) if only says multiple frames are sent together but omits keeping control of the channel (or vice versa).

points.description: States that its purpose is to reduce the overhead of transmitting small frames.
Advantage vs carrier extension: more efficient because single small frames are not padded/filled with extension (garbage) bits, so no wasted bandwidth.
points.partial_credit: Half if says only 'more efficient' without linking to no padding of frames.

points.description: Disadvantage vs carrier extension: needs frames queued/waiting for transmission (buffering), causing delay of frames.
points.partial_credit: Half if only buffering/waiting frames or only delay is stated, not both.

rubric.notes: Full marks need the precise definition (multiple frames concatenated in one transmission without releasing the channel), the small-frame overhead purpose, and one correct advantage and one correct disadvantage versus carrier extension. A vague statement such as 'sends frames faster' earns nothing for that point. A wrong advantage or disadvantage (e.g. claiming it pads frames) earns nothing for that point.
